extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, and fact-checkers interested in misinformation
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and documenting a specific viral misinformation incident (the purported Sweden 'sex competition' story): tracing sources, verifying official statements, and reporting corrections and debunking. Focus is on how the claim circulated, who reported it, and how it was investigated and disproven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of legitimate sources/proof
rubrics_metrics.description: "without providing any legitimate sources, without proof of such a competition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports that publish details (participants, rules) but do not cite legitimate sources or provide proof should be treated as suspect. The page points to Marca publishing rules and participant names without legitimate sourcing as an example of poor reporting practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify official recognition via authoritative bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Swedish Sports Confederation confirmed that the application was not accepted and emphasized that Sweden has not declared sex as a sport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before accepting claims of official recognition (e.g., a country 'declaring' something a sport), check statements from the relevant governing or regulatory body. Official denials or confirmations are decisive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm organizational registration and affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes the absence of any affiliation or collaboration with any sex organization and that the 'Swedish Sex Federation' was an unregistered organization whose membership application was rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether an organization claiming to represent an activity is formally registered or recognized and whether its applications or memberships have been accepted; unregistered or rejected entities are weak evidence for official events or endorsements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine website authenticity and redirections
rubrics_metrics.description: A website bearing the same name exists, although it redirects to a pornography website; it also featured a countdown and an email address linked to the 'Swedish Sex Federation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the domain, ownership, redirects, and content of websites cited by claims. Redirects to unrelated content, countdowns, or amateur contact details (emails) can indicate inauthentic or misleading operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for corrections, removals, and lack of corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publications removed the initial reports after it turned out to be a hoax, while other outlets remain published and some have not corrected their reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track whether original publishers issue corrections or retract stories. Lack of correction or persistent publication of debunked claims is a negative indicator of reporting quality and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult reputable fact-checking and news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputable fact-checking sources including Reuters, Snopes, Mashable, Deutsche Welle, and others investigated and debunked the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use investigations and reporting from established fact-checkers and mainstream news organizations to corroborate or refute viral claims; these sources often trace evidence and provide authoritative debunks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace claims to primary actors and motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation found an individual (Dragan Bratic) who submitted an application seeking classification of sexual activities as a sport and owns several strip clubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and investigate the originators of a claim (individuals or groups), their motives, and their connections; personal or commercial motives (e.g., reputation, publicity) can explain and weaken sensational claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess media circulation and social media spread
rubrics_metrics.description: On various news outlets and social media platforms, news claiming 'Sweden Hosting First-Ever Sex Competition' emerged and generated significant attention; reactions ranged from skepticism to curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map how widely and on which platforms a claim is circulating and analyze public reactions. High virality does not imply truth; understanding spread helps prioritize verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify event-specific details (rules, scoring, participants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marca listed participants' names and reported rules and scoring (judges scoring from five to 10 and by popular audiences), but these details lacked legitimate sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize purported event details for plausibility and sourcing. Detailed-sounding rules or participant lists are not proof—confirm with organizers, regulators, or independent records before publishing.
